items.claim: Construction step 3: place the tip of the compass at another point M₁ and with an opening equal to M₁A draw circle M₁. The circle M₁ passes through point A.

items.quote: Third : Drawing a circle passing through three given points:
items.text: Third : Drawing a circle passing through three given points:

items.quote: Given: A, B and C are three given points on the plane.
items.text: Given: A, B and C are three given points on the plane. R.T.P: Draw circle M passing through the three points A, B and C.

items.quote: (figure: circle M with L1, L2, points A, B, C)
items.caption: Circle with centre M, passing through A, B and C. Line L1 (black, vertical with arrows) is the axis of AB and passes through M; line L2 (pink) is the axis of BC and passes through M. C is at top left, B at bottom left, A at bottom right of the circle. Right-angle marks and equal-length tick marks are shown on AB and BC.

items.quote: Construction:
items.claim: Construction:

items.quote: Draw the straight line L1 axis of AB thus M ∈ L1 .
items.claim: Draw the straight line $L_1$, the axis of $\overline{AB}$, thus $M \in L_1$.

items.quote: Draw the straight line L2 axis of BC thus M ∈ L2 .
items.claim: Draw the straight line $L_2$, the axis of $\overline{BC}$, thus $M \in L_2$.

items.quote: If L1 ∩ L2 = {M}, state the tip of the compass at point M
items.claim: If $L_1 \cap L_2 = \{M\}$, place the tip of the compass at point M with an opening equalling MA. Draw the circle M. You will find it passing through the two points B and C.

items.quote: If L1 ∩ L2 = φ , can you identify the position of point M ?
items.text: If $L_1 \cap L_2 = \phi$, can you identify the position of point M? Explain your answer.

items.quote: If A, B, and C are collinear then L1 // L2 and L1 ∩ L2 = φ
items.claim: If A, B and C are collinear then $L_1 \parallel L_2$ and $L_1 \cap L_2 = \phi$.

items.quote: A circle cannot be drawn passing through the three points A, B, and C.
items.claim: A circle cannot be drawn passing through the three points A, B and C (when collinear).

items.quote: (figure: collinear C, B, A with L2 and L1)
items.caption: Horizontal line through collinear points C, B, A (left to right) with tick marks showing equal segments; two parallel vertical lines L2 (axis of CB, between C and B) and L1 (axis of BA, between B and A) with right-angle marks, never meeting.

items.quote: From the previous, we deduce that :
items.text: From the previous, we deduce that :

items.quote: There is one and only one circle which passes through three noncollinear points.
items.claim: There is one and only one circle which passes through three noncollinear points.

items.quote: Using the geometric tools and draw the triangle A B C in which AB = 4 cm,
items.text: Using the geometric tools draw the triangle ABC in which AB = 4 cm, BC = 5 cm and CA = 6 cm. Draw circle passing through the points A, B and C. What is the kind of triangle ABC with respect to the measures of its angles? Where is the center of the circle located with respect to the triangle?

items.quote: Corollaries
items.text: Corollaries

items.quote: The circle which passes through the vertices of a triangle is called the circumcircle
items.claim: The circle which passes through the vertices of a triangle is called the circumcircle of this triangle.

items.quote: a triangle is inscribed in a circle if its vertices are on the circle
items.claim: A triangle is said to be inscribed in a circle if its vertices are on the circle.

items.quote: The perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle intersect
items.claim: The perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle intersect at a point which is the center of the circumcircle of the triangle.

learning_objectives.label: Circle through one point
learning_objectives.description: Draw circles passing through a given point, choosing centers and using the compass, and state that infinitely many such circles exist (equal radii give centers on a congruent circle centered at A).

learning_objectives.label: Circle through two points
learning_objectives.description: Draw circles passing through two given points using the axis of the chord AB for the center, and determine the possible circles for a given radius or diameter, including the smallest radius.

learning_objectives.label: Circle through three points
learning_objectives.description: Draw the circumcircle through three noncollinear points as the intersection of the axes of two sides, identify its center in the triangle, and explain why collinear points give no circle.
